questions.question:
Any party can be recognized as a national level political party if it-

(i) Get 6% of the total valid votes in the election and 4 seats in the Lok Sabha.

(ii) 2% of the total seats in the Lok Sabha have been obtained in at least three states.

Which of the above statements are/are true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) and (ii) both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A political party must secure at least 6% of the total valid votes polled in any four or more states in a general election to the Lok Sabha or to the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Additionally, the party must win at least 4 seats in the Lok Sabha from any state or states to meet the first criterion.
 
• The second criterion requires the party to win at least 2% of the total seats in the Lok Sabha, with members elected from at least three different states.
 
• Both conditions (i) and (ii) are necessary for a party to be recognized as a national-level political party in India.
 
• These criteria are set by the Election Commission of India, which is the authority responsible for administering election processes in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The ECI is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The Election Commission operates under the authority of the Constitution per Article 324 and subsequently enacted Representation of the People Act.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament, with members directly elected by the people of India.
 
• Elections are held every five years to elect members of the Lok Sabha, unless dissolved sooner.
 
 
 
• **National Party**
 
 
• In India, a national party is a political party that meets certain criteria set by the Election Commission of India, allowing it to be recognized as a national entity.
 
• National parties have the privilege of using a unique party symbol across the country.
 
• They also receive time slots for campaign advertisements on state-owned television and radio stations during elections.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Political Parties**
 
 
• The recognition of political parties in India as national or state parties is governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.
 
• The recognition status provides several benefits, including reserved party symbols, free broadcast time on state media, and access to electoral rolls.
 
• Recognition is reviewed periodically based on the performance of the parties in elections.

questions.question: Which of the following languages were declared as the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Bill, 2020?

options.text: Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi, and English

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi, and English**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Bill, 2020 declares Kashmiri, Dogri, Urdu, Hindi, and English as the official languages of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• These languages are to be used for official purposes and in the business of the Legislative Assembly of the union territory.
 
• The Administrator of the Union Territory has the authority to notify the effective date for the implementation of these languages.
 
• English is clarified to remain in use for administrative and legislative purposes as it was before the commencement of the Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Jammu and Kashmir Official Languages Bill, 2020 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **September 22, 2020**.
 
• The official languages include **Kashmiri** and **Dogri**, which were not officially recognized previously in this region for government functions.
 
• **Urdu** has historically been one of the official languages in Jammu and Kashmir and continues to be so under this Bill.
 
• The inclusion of **Hindi** reflects the broader use of the language across India, ensuring better integration with the central government.
 
• English continues to serve as a medium for official communication, facilitating national and international interactions.
 
• This Bill aims to accommodate linguistic diversity while maintaining administrative efficiency in the Union Territory.

questions.question: Which of the following is the southernmost geographical unit of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The southernmost geographical unit of India is Indira Point.
 
• Indira Point is located on Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It was previously known as Pygmalion Point.
 
• Sadly, Indira Point was submerged by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
 
• Before its submergence, it held the distinction of being the southernmost point of the Indian Union.
 
• Kanyakumari is often considered the southernmost point of India, but this refers to the southernmost point of the Indian mainland.
 
• India's geography is diverse, encompassing a vast peninsula, islands, and a diverse range of terrains.
 
• Understanding geographical extremities helps to appreciate the country's vastness and unique location.

questions.question: A party recognised by the Election Commission of India that secures at least ________ of the total votes in the General Election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly in four or more states in addition to winning four Lok Sabha seats is called a National Party.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**six per cent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A party is recognized as a National Party by the Election Commission of India if it secures at least **six per cent of the total votes** in the General Election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly in four or more states.
 
• In addition to the vote percentage, the party must also win at least **four Lok Sabha seats**.
 
• Recognition as a National Party provides the party with several privileges, including a common symbol for candidates across India.
 
• National parties have the ability to influence national politics and policies due to their significant presence across multiple states.
 
• As of the latest information, India has eight recognized National Parties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Party Recognition:**

 
 
• To be recognized as a State Party, a party must secure at least six per cent of the total votes in the Legislative Assembly or Lok Sabha elections in that state.
 
• It must also win at least two seats in the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
 
 
• **Symbol Allocation:**
 
 
• National and State Parties are granted exclusive symbols for their candidates.
 
• Independent candidates and unrecognized parties can choose from a list of free symbols.
 
 
 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI):**
 
 
• The ECI is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India.
 
• It ensures free and fair elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice President.
 
 
 
• **Privileges of National Parties:**
 
 
• National Parties are entitled to broadcast/telecast facilities during elections on public broadcasters Doordarshan and All India Radio.
 
• They are also allowed to consult with the ECI regarding the dates of elections and other important electoral matters.

questions.question: According to Article 343 (1) of the Constitution of India, Hindi written in the Hindi script shall be the official language of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Devanagari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Devanagari is an alphasyllabary used in India and Nepal for languages such as Hindi, Marathi, Nepali, and Sanskrit.
 
• The script consists of 14 vowels and 33 consonants and is written from left to right.
 
• Devanagari script is highly phonetic, meaning that each character represents a specific sound.
 
• It is one of the most widely used and adopted writing systems in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 343 (1) of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• Article 343(1) states that the official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
 
• The form of numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union shall be the international form of Indian numerals.
 
• This article was adopted to promote a uniform language for the administration across the country.
 
 
 
• **Kharosthi Script**
 
 
• Kharosthi is an ancient script used in Gandhara, an ancient region in present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• It was used to write the Gandhari language and was in use from the 4th century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script**
 
 
• Brahmi is one of the oldest writing systems in South Asia, dating back to the 3rd century BCE.
 
• It is considered the mother of many modern Indian scripts, including Devanagari.
 
 
 
• **Indus Script**
 
 
• The Indus script is a writing system developed by the Indus Valley Civilization during the Bronze Age.
 
• It remains undeciphered and is one of the oldest known scripts in the world.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?

options.text: A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India follows a multi-party system where multiple political parties can exist and participate in elections.
 
• Political parties in India are classified into national, state or regional level based on their performance and influence.
 
• National parties are those that have influence over a larger part of India, while state or regional parties have influence limited to specific states or regions.
 
• This classification helps in managing the democratic process and ensuring representation at both the national and state levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The ECI ensures free and fair elections in India.
 
 
 
• **Registration of Political Parties**
 
 
• Political parties in India are registered with the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
• Registration with the ECI is a precondition for a political party to be recognized as a national or state party.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Political Parties**
 
 
• The status of a political party, whether national or state, is determined based on its performance in elections.
 
• Criteria for recognition include the number of seats won in elections and the percentage of votes obtained.
 
 
 
• **Symbols of Political Parties**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India assigns symbols to political parties to help voters identify them during elections.
 
• Symbols play a significant role in the election process, especially for illiterate voters who may not recognize party names.

questions.question: In which year did the Indian Constitution declare Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1949**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindi in Devanagari script** was declared the official language of the Union of India in **1949**.
 
• This declaration is enshrined in **Article 343** of the Constitution of India.
 
• According to this article, Hindi in Devanagari script would be used for official purposes of the Union, while the international form of Indian numerals would be used for official purposes.
 
• The Constituent Assembly adopted this provision on **14th September 1949**, which is now celebrated as **Hindi Diwas** every year.
 
• The Constitution also allowed for the continued use of English for official purposes for a period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution, which could be extended by legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
